issues.reason: The idiom coherence test rules the literal reading out (nothing occupies the physical edge of an abstract state), so minting `(Member sk_verge_1 verge)` is the `(Member sk_bean_1 bean)` failure the idiom rule names by example — a physical object the text never introduces.

`(On <entity> <entity>)` is the entity-attached surface-preposition head for a thing POSITIONED on another thing, so the atom asserts a spatial fact that is false of the cat, and the sentence's actual claim (imminent starvation) is nowhere recorded.

It stands that `verge` fails the verb-paraphrase test and so is not a nominalization whose of-phrase takes the `Of` oblique; it is overstated in prescribing `PartOf` / `Possession`, since `(PartOf sk_verge_1 starvation)` would be at least as false — the atom's real defect is the literal reading that issue 0 already names.

gaps_confirmed: imminent / prospective aspect — "on the verge of X", "about to V", "on the point of V-ing": a state nearly but not yet reached has no licensed operator (`Future` would wrongly assert the eventuality occurs)
new_gaps: predicative PP idioms ("on the verge of X", "in trouble", "out of order") have no slot: the idiom rule's single surface symbol is shaped for a verb+object event class or a kind, and the entity-attached surface preposition asserts a spatial position instead

affective / evaluative attributive modifiers — "the poor cat" means pitiable, not impoverished — are indistinguishable from descriptive property modifiers, so `(Member sk_cat_1 poor)` records a property the speaker never predicates of the referent
repair_summary: Removed the literal `verge` witness, its `Of` complement and the `(Past (On sk_cat_1 sk_verge_1))` position atom — the idiom coherence test rules the literal reading out and the imminent-aspect gap leaves no licensed replacement, so the predicate is dropped rather than re-encoded. The subject atoms (typing, `poor`) are untouched, and the clause's `Past` goes with the removed predicate since nothing licensed remains to carry it.
notes: I considered a fused idiom property `(Past (Member sk_cat_1 on_the_verge_of_starvation))` and rejected it: "on the verge of X" is a productive frame, not a fixed word string, and the compound section's "leave opaque for now (don't force)" line on adjective/condition compounds tells against minting one — replacing removed content with an invention is barred. The result is a subject-only parse, which is the honest cost of the confirmed gap.
